title: MBB Deck Storyline
description: Schema for storyline JSON consumed by scripts/build_deck.py

governing_thought.description: The single-sentence answer the deck supports (also called the key message). Documented for human review; not directly rendered.

document_type.description: What the document is for. Calibrates validate_storyline.py: 'decision_pre_read' is cover + executive summary + up to four pages; 'board', 'decision_pre_read' and 'external' must close with a 'decisions' slide. See references/storyline.md.

audience.description: Who decides and who influences, and each decision maker's main concern, as free text. Enough for most documents; use 'stakeholders' when several decision makers stand in different places. For review; not rendered.

objective.description: What the audience should do after reading (e.g. 'approval of three decisions on 12 May'). For review; not rendered.

question.description: The one question the complication raises and the governing thought answers. For review; not rendered.

stakeholders.description: OPTIONAL structured audience. Worth filling for decision documents with several decision makers or a contested message; skip it otherwise. For review; not rendered.

current_stage.description: Where they stand on the commitment ladder today.

target_stage.description: Where they must be after this document.

main_concern.description: The objection to answer on a page before it is raised (callout or safeguard).

key_figures.description: OPTIONAL definitions of the headline figures: what each number measures, against which reference, for which period. Worth filling when the governing thought rests on a number. validate_storyline.py checks that each is fully defined, appears on a page in identical form, and reconciles with its components. For review; not rendered.

name.description: Short label, e.g. 'SMB cost to serve'.

value.description: The figure exactly as written on the pages, e.g. '$14M'.

measure.description: What is measured, e.g. 'annual fully loaded cost to serve the SMB tier'.

reference.description: What the figure is stated against: a baseline (budget, prior year, do-nothing case), a benchmark, a target, or 'absolute' for a plain level. Use the reader's own reference.

period.description: The period it covers, e.g. 'FY24' or 'per year from FY27'.

by_when.description: For targets: when it is reached.

lever.description: What produces the effect. Name all levers if several act together.

status.description: How firm the figure is, e.g. 'actual', 'estimate', 'preliminary'.

components.description: The parts the figure is made of, when it is a sum. They must add up to 'value' and share its measure.

name.description: OPTIONAL page name for references ('the savings page'). Metadata only: never rendered on the slide. Must be unique.

title.description: The governing thought as the slide title

framing_line.description: Optional subtitle under the action title — typically methodology, sample size, or logic ('Based on n=240 interviews', 'Acme analysis vs. industry')

supporting_points.description: One point per argument (section), in document order. A point may open with a **bold lead** that mirrors the section's action title, followed by the key numbers.

context.description: Situation and complication in at most two sentences, rendered above the supporting points.

decisions.description: Decision needs, one line each, rendered in their own box. Must match the 'decisions' slide that closes the document.

why_now.description: The deadline or event that forces the decisions.

name.description: OPTIONAL page name for references ('the savings page'). Metadata only: never rendered on the slide. Must be unique.

callout.description: OPTIONAL outlined box above the footer: answers a stakeholder's main concern on the page, or states a caveat (e.g. why a figure differs from one quoted earlier). One or two lines.

label.description: Bold lead, e.g. 'Why this differs from the March figure'.

comparison_type.description: The comparison type of the MESSAGE (not the data shape). Drives the chart-type check in validate_storyline.py: components → stacked column/sorted bar; items → bar/waterfall; time_series → line/column; distribution → column/histogram/line; correlation → scatter/bubble/paired bars.

chart_type.description: Intended chart type (e.g. 'waterfall', 'sorted_bar', 'line', 'scatter'). NOTE: 'pie' is banned in this skill — the skill author's hard rule; components render as stacked columns or sorted bars.

decisions.description: Decision needs and next steps: the closing page of a senior document.
